newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile reports swelling Jan-Oct trade gap.
newsitem.headline: Chile reports swelling Jan-Oct trade gap.

text.p: Chile posted a trade deficit of $824 million for the first 10 months of the year, against a $1.2 billion surplus in the same period of 1995, the central bank said in its fortnightly report.
Booming imports and a fall in commodity exports were the main factors behind the steep rise in the October trade deficit to $487 million from $129 million a year ago, said the report.
"October's figures were the result mainly of the dynamic behavior of imports together with an important fall in exports in the period," it said.
Exports fell last month to $1.2 billion from $1.4 billion in the same month of 1995. Imports swelled to $1.7 billion from $1.5 billion.
Export volumes fell 12 percent compared with October 1995, mainly as the result of a sharp fall in exports other than copper, said the report.
Sharpest falls were seen in bleached wood pulp exports, down 67 percent from a year earlier, molybdenum, down 57 percent, and methanol, down 44 percent.
Copper exports fell 15 percent as the result of a 30 percent drop in world copper prices.
Non-traditional exports, which include salmon and wine, grew 10 percent, but this was not sufficent to make up for the fall in commodity exports.
Capital goods imports grew strongly from a year earlier, boosted by the import of two ships, it said.
Intermediate goods imports rose 7.2 percent, with consumer goods imports up 6.3 percent.
"The consumer goods figure reflects the economic slowdown after growing 24 percent and 11 percent in the second and third quarters this year," said the report.
